thread.title: U.S. Stocks Plunge on Tech Selloff

author: Nikita Medvedev
title: U.S. Stocks Plunge on Tech Selloff
text:
11/19/2018 853
U.S. stocks plunged on Monday morning led by a major decline in the tech sector. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell by over 400 points or 1.57% in late morning trading session. The S&P 500 Index fell by 1.55%, while the Nasdaq Composite also lagged behind, falling 2.59%.
The market continued to fall after a report from Apple’s (NASDAQ: AAPL) supplier, Lumentum, did not provide a sales forecast for the Company last week. Lumentum’s report indicated weaker sales for Apple, which sent its stock falling 5% last week. Apple shares continued to slip on Monday, falling by 3.96%.
The tech sector saw a selloff on Monday as Amazon.com, (NASDAQ: AMZN) shares fell by 4.01%, Facebook (NASDAQ: FB) shares fell by 4.54%, Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX) shares fell by 4% and Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) shares fell by 2.67%.
The sector continued to fall after Nvidia Corporation (NASDAQ: NVDA) reported its quarterly earnings last Thursday. Nvidia missed revenue estimates, causing shares to plummet by 15%. Shares continued to fall on Monday, falling by 6.3%. JD.com (NASDAQ: JD) reported its quarterly earnings before market open on Monday, also missing estimates, which sent shares tumbling 3.5%.
“It’s going to require a recovery in tech to make things happen,” said Greg Luken, Chief Executive Officer of Luken Investment Analytics, according to CNBC. “I think where we are in tech, we’re going to see tough sledding towards the end of the year. I think stocks that are down will see further selling pressure.”
The market was also fueled by oil price slumps , as they headed for the biggest slip since 2009. West Texas Intermediate crude fell by 1.4% to USD 55.67 a barrel, down more than 14% for November.
Rising mortgage rates and continued home price growth also contributed to the overall market decline on Monday. Sentiment among homebuilders dropped 8 points in November to 60 in the National Association of Home Builders/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index. The drop is lowest reading since August 2016, but according to CNBC, any level above 50 is still considered positive.
“Builders report that they continue to see signs of consumer demand for new homes but that customers are taking a pause due to concerns over rising interest rates and home prices,” said NAHB Chairman Randy Noel, a builder from LaPlace, Louisiana.
Despite U.S. markets plunging, global markets were mixed on Monday The U.K.’s FTSE 100 was down 0.19%, Germany’s DAX Index fell by 0.85% and Paris’ CAC 40 fell by 0.79% due to ongoing Brexit issues. Meanwhile, Asia markets climbed, as Hong Kong’s Hang Seng index climbed by 0.72%, the Shanghai Index rose by 0.91%, Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 gained 0.65% and Korea’s KOSPI Index rose by 0.39%.
